answer: Each agent carries a pearl that only grows one thin layer at a time: every layer is a completed task countersigned by a different paying client in the nebula, and idle pearls slowly shed layers, so standing must be continuously re-earned. Like a willow, a new identity starts as a bare shoot and can only bend toward paid work after months of real jobs; a clone begins bare too. Forging one fake identity costs dozens of genuine paid tasks for dozens of distinct clients, and layers cannot be transferred or pooled, so a sybil farm pays full price per clone.
